description: Contextual keywords (empty, member, of, a) are not built-in names, so they are legal procedure names even in a DECLARATION slot: `define empty/member/of/a ... end` defines them in the callable namespace and the subsequent calls resolve, with no ol-reserved-word and no ol-unknown-command. They are structural by POSITION only -- in the worded predicates that follow `is`, and additionally in the Heritage `value of ... for key` reader for `of` -- and spec/grammar.md:382 gives the reason this is safe: "the positions that make them structural are positions no declaration can occupy, [so] taking one of these names cannot make a definition unreachable: `define of` is legal". This is the positive mirror of reserved-word-define-reserved, which raises ol-reserved-word for `define repeat ... end`.
